name: APT3
affiliation_detail:
Associated to Guangzhou Boyu Information Technology Company Limited (Boyusec), operating as a contractor for China's Ministry of State Security. 
Boyusec was co-founded by Wu Yingzhuo and Dong Hao, both later indicted by the U.S. DOJ (Intrustion Truth, 2017; DOJ 2017). Boyusec collaborated with Guangdong Information Technology Security Evaluation Center (Guangdong ITSEC), a field office of CNITSEC, which is run by the MSS (Recorded Future, 2017).
No DOJ indictment or formal government attribution to a specific buereau or unit has been published.
entity_name: Guangzhou Boyu Information Technology Co., Ltd. (Boyusec)
description:
APT3 is a state-sponsored group attributed to the Ministry of State Security (MSS), operating through the entity Guangzhou Boyu Information Technology Company (Boyusec) as a contractor.
Active from at least 2009 to mid-2017, the group initially targeted a broad range of U.S. organizations across the defense, telecommunications, transportation, technology, and aerospace sectors for the goal of intellectual property extraction, before shifting focus to political organizations in Hong Kong around mid-2015. (Intrustion Truth, 2017; Symantec, 2015)
APT3 was notable for its technical sophistication, including the use of zero-day exploits in Internet Explorer and Adobe Flash, and was discovered to have obtained and used variants of NSA Equation Group tools (DoublePulsar) at least a year before the Shadow Brokers leak.
The group was responsible for Operations Clandestine Fox, Clandestine Wolf, and Double Tap. In May 2017, Intrusion Truth linked APT3 to Boyusec and the MSS, corroborated by Recorded Future and FireEye. The DOJ indicted three Boyusec employees in November 2017, and Boyusec was subsequently disbanded. 
APT3 activity has not been observed since May 2017. (Intrusion Truth, 2017; WSJ, 2017)

campaigns.name: Operation Clandestine Fox
campaigns.description: APT3 exploited a zero-day vulnerability in Internet Explorer (CVE-2014-1776, affecting versions 9 through 11) in targeted attacks against U.S. organizations. The group used spear-phishing emails to deliver exploits and deployed the Pirpi backdoor via DLL side-loading using a legitimate Chrome binary. FireEye published a follow-up "Clandestine Fox Part Deux" documenting the group's rapid adaptation after initial disclosure.

sources.title: New Zero-Day Exploit targeting Internet Explorer Versions 9 through 11

campaigns.name: Operation Double Tap
campaigns.description: APT3 used two known vulnerabilities (CVE-2014-6332 in Windows OLE and CVE-2014-4113 in Windows kernel) in a spear-phishing campaign. The group established persistence via registry Run keys and startup folder scripts, used PowerShell for payload delivery, and employed SOCKS5-based multi-stage C2 channels. This represented a shift toward using known exploits combined with social engineering rather than zero-days.

campaigns.name: Operation Clandestine Wolf
campaigns.description: APT3 exploited an Adobe Flash Player zero-day vulnerability (CVE-2015-3113) as part of a phishing campaign targeting organizations in the U.S. aerospace, defense, construction and engineering, technology, telecommunications, and transportation sectors, as well as U.S. government agencies.

sources.title: Operation Clandestine Wolf – Adobe Flash Zero-Day in APT3 Phishing Campaign

campaigns.name: Hong Kong targeting shift
campaigns.description: Around mid-2015, APT3 shifted its primary targeting from U.S. organizations to political organizations and entities in Hong Kong. Symantec documented this shift in September 2016. The change may have been partially driven by increased U.S.-China tensions and the 2015 Obama-Xi cyber agreement.

sources.title: Buckeye cyberespionage group shifts gaze from US to Hong Kong

campaigns.name: Siemens, Moody's Analytics, and Trimble intrusions (DOJ Indictment)
campaigns.description: Three Boyusec employees (Wu Yingzhuo, Dong Hao, Xia Lei) conducted sustained intrusions against Siemens AG, Moody's Analytics, and GPS/surveying company Trimble Inc., stealing hundreds of gigabytes of sensitive data including trade secrets, proprietary technology, and confidential business information in the finance, engineering, and technology sectors. Wu hacked Trimble, Dong hacked Siemens, and Xia hacked Moody's Analytics.

sources.title: United States of America v. Wu Yingzhuo, Dong Hao, Xia Lei

campaigns.name: Equation Group tool usage campaign
campaigns.description: Beginning March 2016, APT3 deployed a variant of the NSA Equation Group's DoublePulsar backdoor via its custom Bemstour exploit tool—at least a year before the Shadow Brokers leaked these tools publicly. Initial attacks targeted organizations in Hong Kong, followed by targets in Belgium, Luxembourg, Vietnam, and the Philippines. The DoublePulsar variant differed from the later leaked version, suggesting APT3 may have reverse-engineered it from captured network traffic. Bemstour and DoublePulsar continued to be used until at least September 2018, after APT3's apparent dissolution, raising questions about tool handoff to other groups.

sources.title: Buckeye: Espionage Outfit Used Equation Group Tools Prior to Shadow Brokers Leak
